mainTopic: Finding a תנא who holds that neither עקירה nor הנחה needs a 4x4 area: first רבי עקיבא, then רבי
overview: Earlier, רבה explained the case of a hand in the משנה using רבי עקיבא's rule that an object in the air counts as resting (קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא). The גמרא first objects that רבה himself once asked a בעיא about this. Do רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue below ten טפחים, about קלוטה? Or do they argue above ten, about learning זורק from מושיט? The answer is that רבה later resolved his doubt: רבי עקיבא holds קלוטה. Then a new problem arises. קלוטה only shows that הנחה needs no 4x4 area, while עקירה might still need one. So רב יוסף says instead that the משנה follows רבי. The גמרא looks for a source. The ברייתא of the tiny ledge (זיז) is pushed away with אביי's explanation: the case is tree branches, and רבי holds שדי נופו בתר עיקרו. Next comes a ברייתא about throwing across a רשות היחיד, where שמואל says רבי makes him liable twice, implying no 4x4 is needed for either עקירה or הנחה. The amud ends as the גמרא starts to reject this proof with a statement of רב and שמואל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge: רבה himself was unsure where they argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה's assumption that רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about an object passing within ten טפחים. רבה himself raised this as an open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it really within ten handbreadths that they argue? But רבה himself raised this as an unresolved question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's earlier explanation. That explanation assumed the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן is about an object below ten טפחים, but רבה himself was unsure about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's explanation of the hand in the משנה depends on רבי עקיבא holding קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא below ten טפחים. If רבה once treated this as an open question (a בעיא), then he cannot simply build on it. The next steps quote his question to prove the point.

keyTerms.meaning: Within ten handbreadths (טפחים) of the ground
They argue / disagree
He raised it as an unresolved question (a בעיא)
The אמורא whose explanation is being examined

phrases.english: And is it within ten handbreadths that they disagree?
phrases.notes: Questions the assumption behind רבה's earlier explanation

phrases.english: But Rabba himself raised this as a dilemma!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה פְּלִיגִי? וְהָא מִיבַּעְיָא בָּעֵי לַהּ רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's explanation from the previous part of the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's assumption that רבי עקיבא holds קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, which shows the argument is about a case within ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה cannot rely on a premise that he himself raised as an unresolved בעיא

steps.title: רבה's dilemma, first side: they argue below ten
steps.stepSummary: The first possibility in רבה's בעיא. The argument is below ten טפחים, and it is about קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא. Above ten, everyone agrees the thrower is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה asked: Do they argue below ten handbreadths? If so, this is their disagreement: רבי עקיבא holds that an object in the air is treated as if it were resting, and the רבנן hold that we do not say this. But above ten handbreadths, everyone agrees the thrower is exempt, because everyone agrees we do not learn throwing from handing over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first side of רבה's question. Maybe the argument about throwing across a public domain is only below ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is throwing from one private domain to another across a public domain. On this side, רבי עקיבא makes the thrower liable because the object, while flying through the public domain's air, already counts as resting there. Above ten טפחים the air is not part of the public domain, so everyone exempts. On this side, nobody compares זורק to מושיט.

keyTerms.meaning: Below ten handbreadths, the airspace that belongs to the public domain
An object 'caught' in the air is treated as if it had come to rest
One who throws
One who hands over or passes an object by hand
We derive / learn one law from another

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. מושיט means handing an object across by hand, which is liable even above ten טפחים because of a special source. זורק means throwing it, and the question is whether it follows the same law.

phrases.english: For Rabba asked:
Do they disagree below ten handbreadths?
And this is what they disagree about:
Rabbi Akiva holds
an object in the air is considered as if it was placed down,
and the Rabbis hold that we do not say
an object in the air is considered as if it was placed down.
But above ten handbreadths
everyone agrees he is exempt,
and according to everyone we do not derive
throwing from handing over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the בעיא that the קשיא referred to, as support for the challenge
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן below ten טפחים, about קלוטה, or above ten טפחים, about learning זורק from מושיט?

steps.title: רבה's dilemma, second side: they argue above ten
steps.stepSummary: The second possibility in רבה's בעיא. The argument is above ten טפחים, about learning זורק from מושיט. Below ten, everyone holds the thrower liable because of קלוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps they argue above ten handbreadths. If so, this is their disagreement: רבי עקיבא holds we learn throwing from handing over, and the רבנן hold we do not. But below ten handbreadths, everyone agrees he is liable. Why? Because we say an object in the air is treated as if it were resting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבה's question with the opposite possibility. On this side, everyone agrees to קלוטה, so it is not a special view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this side, קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא is accepted by everyone below ten טפחים. The argument moves above ten, to whether זורק can be learned from מושיט. Since רבה raised this as an open question, the challenge seems strong: how could he know that קלוטה is רבי עקיבא's position, as opposed to everyone's? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps, introducing the second side of a question
Above ten handbreadths, outside the public domain's airspace
Liable
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Or perhaps they disagree above ten handbreadths,
and this is what they disagree about:
Rabbi Akiva holds
we derive throwing from handing over,
and the Rabbis hold
we do not derive throwing from handing over.
But below ten handbreadths
everyone agrees he is liable.
What is the reason?
We say an object in the air is considered as if it was placed down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of רבה's בעיא, which completes the support for the קשיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קלוטה is accepted by everyone below ten טפחים, with the argument above ten being about זורק and מושיט

steps.title: Answer: רבה later resolved his dilemma
steps.stepSummary: No difficulty. After raising the question, רבה later resolved it: רבי עקיבא is the one who holds קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a difficulty. After he raised the question, he later resolved it for himself: רבי עקיבא holds that an object in the air is treated as if it were resting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבה's question came first, and he later settled it on the first side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements of רבה do not contradict each other because they come from different times. Once רבה decided that the argument is below ten טפחים and that קלוטה is רבי עקיבא's view, he could use it to explain the hand in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult, introducing an answer
After it was asked as a question
It was later resolved for him

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's final view is that רבי עקיבא holds קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, and the רבנן disagree. This lets him explain the hand within ten טפחים according to רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
after it was asked as a dilemma
it was later resolved for him
that Rabbi Akiva holds
an object in the air is considered as if it was placed down.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: בָּתַר דְּאִיבַּעְיָא הֲדַר אִיפְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the question came first and was resolved later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's open question shows he could not rely on רבי עקיבא holding קלוטה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה later decided that רבי עקיבא holds קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, so his explanation of the משנה stands

steps.title: New challenge: maybe only lifting needs a 4x4 area
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי עקיבא holds קלוטה, perhaps that only shows הנחה does not need a 4x4 area. עקירה might still need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is only placing down that does not need a four-by-four area, while lifting up does need it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רבה's comparison. רבי עקיבא's rule may only teach something about putting down, not about lifting up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קלוטה proves that an object can count as 'put down' even without resting on a 4x4 surface. The משנה's case, however, also involves lifting an object from a hand, which has no 4x4 area. Perhaps עקירה, the beginning and core of the מלאכה, has stricter requirements than הנחה, its ending.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing down, the final stage of carrying
Lifting up, the first stage of carrying
Requires (here: a 4x4 area)
But perhaps, introducing a challenge

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that עקירה and הנחה, the two halves of the מלאכה of carrying, may need different conditions. A proof about one half does not automatically apply to the other.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is placing that does not require (a four-by-four area),
but lifting does require it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא הַנָּחָה הוּא דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא, הָא עֲקִירָה בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 4 but challenges how far רבי עקיבא's rule reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: Using קלוטה to show that a hand needs no 4x4 area for both עקירה and הנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קלוטה only addresses placing down. Lifting up may still require a 4x4 area, so the proof does not cover the משנה's case of lifting from a hand

steps.title: רב יוסף: The משנה Follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: After the רבי עקיבא suggestion fell apart, רב יוסף proposes that the משנה follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Whose view is this? It is רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The last attempt to identify the author of the משנה failed. So רב יוסף offers a new answer: the author is רבי, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are looking for a תנא who holds that neither עקירה nor הנחה needs a 4x4 area. That is what the hand case in the משנה implies. רבי עקיבא only covered הנחה, so רב יוסף switches to רבי, who supposedly holds this for both.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach and starts a new one)
Whose opinion is this?
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Whose view is this? It is Rebbi.
phrases.notes: "This" refers to our משנה, which implies no 4x4 is needed for עקירה or הנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the רבי עקיבא identification, which was undermined in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New attribution of the משנה to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, based on קלוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי, who supposedly requires no minimum area for either עקירה or הנחה.

steps.title: Which Ruling of רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי shows that no 4x4 area is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי do you mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רב יוסף to point to the specific ruling of רבי that he is relying on. This sets up the next step, which proposes a candidate source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "it's רבי" means nothing without a source. The גמרא wants a specific ruling of רבי that proves he does not require a 4x4 area.

keyTerms.meaning: Which?

phrases.english: Which [ruling of] Rebbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רב יוסף's attribution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific ruling of רבי that shows he does not require a 4x4 area.

steps.title: Proposed Source: The Small Projection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא where an object landed on a זיז of any size: רבי holds the thrower liable, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is this ruling of רבי, as it was taught: If one threw an object and it landed on a projection of any size, רבי holds him liable and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source. In a ברייתא, an object landed on a tiny ledge, and רבי still made the thrower liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי makes him liable even when the landing spot is tiny, it looks like he does not need a 4x4 area. That would back up רב יוסף. The word אילימא ("if you say") hints that this source will be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposal that is usually about to be rejected)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A projection or ledge sticking out from a wall
Of any size, even tiny

steps.confusionAlert: אילימא does not introduce the גמרא's final answer. It introduces a suggestion that the גמרא is about to knock down.

phrases.english: If you say it is this [ruling of] Rebbi, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: זָרַק וְנָח עַל גַּבֵּי זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא —
phrases.english: One threw, and it landed on a projection of any size —
Rebbi holds him liable, and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a candidate answer to the question "which רבי?"
steps.raayaObject: That רבי does not require a 4x4 area for הנחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the זיז כל שהוא, where רבי holds the thrower liable.

steps.title: אביי: The Case Is a Tree with Branches Leaning Out
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Following אביי, the ברייתא is about a tree standing in רשות היחיד whose branches lean into רשות הרבים, and the object landed on the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case is as we will explain later, following אביי. אביי said: The case is a tree standing in רשות היחיד whose branches lean into רשות הרבים. Someone threw an object, and it landed on the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The ברייתא is not about a random tiny ledge. It is about tree branches attached to a tree that stands in רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case is redefined, the "tiny landing spot" may not really be tiny. The branches might count as part of the tree's trunk, which is a full private domain. So the ברייתא may not prove anything about a size requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Later on, further in the סוגיא
A tree
Its branches or boughs
Private domain

phrases.english: There, it is as we will need to say later, following Abaye,
for Abaye said:
Here, it is about a tree standing in a private domain
and its branches lean into the public domain,
and he threw, and it landed on its branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the זיז ברייתא by redefining its case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the זיז ברייתא as a source for רב יוסף's claim. It does not yet reject the attribution to רבי itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the case was a tiny, independent landing spot. In fact it is tree branches connected to a full private domain.

steps.title: The Real Dispute: Do Branches Follow the Trunk?
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds שדי נופו בתר עיקרו, so the branches count as part of the trunk. The רבנן disagree. The dispute has nothing to do with a 4x4 requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי holds: we say "cast its branches after its trunk." And the רבנן hold: we do not say "cast its branches after its trunk."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי and the רבנן really argue about in the tree case. They disagree on whether the branches are treated as part of the trunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, landing on the branches is like landing on the trunk, and the trunk is a full private domain of 4x4. So he is liable because the trunk-area is large enough, not because he drops the size requirement. Therefore the ברייתא cannot prove that רבי needs no 4x4, and רב יוסף still needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: Cast its branches after its trunk: the branches are treated as part of the trunk
Its trunk or base
We say (we apply this principle)

steps.whatToRemember: The זיז ברייתא does not prove that רבי ignores the 4x4 requirement. His ruling comes from שדי נופו בתר עיקרו: the branches count as the trunk, which is a full private domain. רב יוסף's attribution to רבי still needs a different source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a ruling that looks like it proves a principle can be explained by a completely different principle. Here the principle is about attachment, not size.

phrases.english: For Rebbi holds:
We say: "Cast its branches after its trunk."
And the Rabbis hold:
We do not say: "Cast its branches after its trunk."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי סָבַר אָמְרִינַן שְׁדִי נוֹפוֹ בָּתַר עִיקָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rejection by explaining the true basis of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully removes the זיז ברייתא as evidence that רבי dispenses with the 4x4 requirement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's liability comes from treating the branches as the trunk (a full private domain), not from waiving the minimum area.

steps.title: A new proof from an object thrown across a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different source for רבי: a ברייתא where someone throws from רשות הרבים to רשות הרבים, passing over a רשות היחיד. רבי holds him liable, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף meant this teaching of רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone threw an object from a public domain to a public domain, and a private domain was in the middle, רבי holds him liable and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The זיז proof failed, so the גמרא offers a new teaching of רבי that might show he does not require a 4x4 area. This step only quotes the ברייתא. The explanation of why it proves the point comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object never rested anywhere inside the רשות היחיד. It only flew through the air above it. If רבי still holds the thrower liable, he must treat passing through the air of a domain as if the object 'landed' there, even though there is no 4x4 surface.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals a new attempt after the earlier one was pushed aside.
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Public domain
Private domain
Holds liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The thrower started and ended in רשות הרבים. Nothing ever rested in the רשות היחיד. The whole question is whether flying through its air can count as bringing the object into it and taking it out of it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is this [teaching of] Rabbi, as it was taught:
phrases.notes: A replacement source for רב יוסף's claim that the משנה follows רבי.

phrases.english: If one threw from the public domain to the public domain
and a private domain was in the middle
phrases.notes: The object flew through the air above the private domain.

phrases.english: Rabbi holds him liable, and the Sages exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the זיז ברייתא, which was rejected in steps 9-10, with a new source for רבי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה (which needs no 4x4 area) follows רבי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about throwing from רשות הרבים to רשות הרבים with a רשות היחיד in the middle

steps.title: Two liabilities show that no 4x4 area is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says רבי makes the thrower liable twice: once for bringing in and once for taking out. The גמרא concludes that רבי needs no 4x4 area for either lifting or placing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי held him liable for two [חטאות], one for carrying out and one for carrying in. So it seems that רבי does not require the lifting or the placing to be on a place of 4 by 4.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא proves the point. רבי counts two separate violations, and the גמרא draws the inference that neither one needs a 4x4 area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the object enters the air of the רשות היחיד, it is treated as 'placed' there (הכנסה). When it leaves that air into רשות הרבים, it is treated as 'lifted' from there (הוצאה). The air has no 4x4 surface, so if both the הנחה and the עקירה count, רבי must not require 4x4 for either one.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out from a private domain to a public domain
Carrying in from a public domain to a private domain
Apparently / this shows that. It introduces an inference.
Lifting an object from its place, the start of a forbidden carrying
Placing an object down, the end of a forbidden carrying

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof looks stronger than the זיז proof because it covers both עקירה and הנחה. The very next step, however, begins to push it away using a statement of רב and שמואל about this same dispute.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Rabbi would hold him liable for two [sin-offerings]:
one for carrying out,
phrases.notes: Taking the object out of the private domain's air into the public domain.

phrases.english: and one for carrying in.
phrases.notes: Bringing the object from the public domain into the private domain's air.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה וְלָא הַנָּחָה
phrases.english: Apparently, he requires neither lifting nor placing

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.english: upon a place of four by four [handbreadths].

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא לָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה וְלָא הַנָּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 11 and draws the inference about the 4x4 requirement from it.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי requires no 4x4 area for עקירה or הנחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: רבי holds the thrower liable twice, for הוצאה and for הכנסה

steps.title: Setting up a challenge from what רב and שמואל said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof by pointing out that רב and שמואל both made a statement about this very dispute. Their actual words come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this [dispute] that רב and שמואל both said:
